## The symptom

An agent finishes a fix, waits for it to go live with the documented idiom —
`deploy:await { sha: '<my commit>' }` (or the raw `events:await({ event:
'release:deployed', payload_filter: { sha } })`) — and the wait **times out**
despite the fix genuinely shipping: `git merge-base --is-ancestor <mySha> HEAD`
on the release checkout confirms it, the operator's `/api/health` reports the
expected build, origin/main is fast-forwarded past it. The deploy landed; the
wait just never woke.

## The root cause: exact-sha match against a BATCHED fast-forward

The auto-serve pipeline (`system:release-trigger`) doesn't deploy "the next
commit" — it deploys **whatever green `main` currently points to**, which by
the time the 15-minute tick fires (or the previous deploy's lock releases) is
very often several commits AHEAD of any one agent's fix, because a shared tree
under a busy fleet keeps advancing. The deploy-landed emitter
(`apps/operator/lib/release/deploy.ts`) fired:

```ts
const payload = { sha: plan.targetSha, commits: plan.commits.length, migrations: plan.migrations };
await deps.emitEvent({ key: 'release:deployed', summary, payload, source: 'release-gate' });
await deps.emitEvent({ key: `release:deployed:${plan.targetSha}`, summary, payload, source: 'release-gate' });
```

`plan.targetSha` is **only the tip** of the fast-forward range. If your fix
landed at commit `009fa1d` but three more commits landed on `main` before the
next deploy tick, the deploy ships sha `2a7c61a` — an exact-match wait on
`009fa1d` (via either the per-sha key `release:deployed:009fa1d…` that
`deploy:await{sha}` builds, or a raw payload_filter `{ sha: '009fa1d…' }`
against the global key) **never fires**, because `payload.sha` is always the
tip, never an intermediate commit — even though your commit unquestionably
shipped (it's an ancestor of what deployed).

This is a systemic strand risk for the *officially recommended* idiom
(`deploy:await`'s own description says "Pass sha to target a specific
commit") — it silently fails in exactly the situation (a busy, multi-agent
tree) where an agent is most likely to need it.

## The fix (EI-14601)

`deploy.ts`/`git-ops.ts` now compute the **full-length sha of every commit** in
the deployed range (`commitShasBetween`, a `git rev-list from..to` — distinct
from the existing `commitsBetween`, which returns `--oneline` ABBREVIATED
one-liners not safe for exact-sha keying), and the deploy-landed emit fires the
per-sha key `release:deployed:<sha>` for **every commit the batch included**,
not only the tip:

```ts
for (const sha of plan.commitShas) {
  if (sha === plan.targetSha) continue; // already emitted above
  await deps.emitEvent({ key: `release:deployed:${sha}`, ... });
}
```

So `deploy:await { sha: '009fa1d…' }` now wakes correctly even when the deploy
that actually ships it is several commits ahead. The raw
`events:await({ payload_filter: { sha } })` idiom against the **global** key is
*not* fixed by this (the global emit's payload still carries only the tip
sha) — prefer the per-sha key (`deploy:await{sha}` or
`events:await({ event: 'release:deployed:<sha>' })`) over a payload_filter on
the global key for an exact-commit wait.

## The lesson: an auto-serve/batching pipeline breaks exact-identity waits

Any "wait until X is live" primitive that key/filters on an **exact
identifier** is suspect the moment the thing doing the shipping can **batch
multiple X's into one delivery** and only reports the batch's tip/summary
identifier. Before trusting an exact-match wait against a batching pipeline,
check: does the emit carry identifiers for the whole batch, or just the
outcome's tip? If just the tip, either widen the emit (as here) or fall back
to an ancestry check (`git merge-base --is-ancestor`) instead of exact
equality — never assume "my item's own id will show up in the payload."
